country.name: Malaysia
country.kicker: Two shores. Many identities. Shared connections.

overview.summary: A federation spanning a peninsula and northern Borneo. Malaysia connects busy sea lanes, electronics factories, and culturally varied communities. The sea between its two regions is central to understanding the country.
overview.geography: Peninsular Malaysia sits between Thailand and Singapore. Across the South China Sea, Sabah and Sarawak occupy northern Borneo, sharing the island with Indonesia and Brunei.

whyItMatters.title: Inside everyday electronics
whyItMatters.text: Its manufacturing networks help make the components and devices used far beyond Southeast Asia.

whyItMatters.title: One country, distinct regions
whyItMatters.text: The peninsula, Sabah, and Sarawak bring different histories and communities into a shared federation.

stories.summary: A national border can tell a story that a coastline cannot.

sections.title: A peninsula and an island
sections.text: The western region occupies the southern Malay Peninsula. Sabah and Sarawak lie on Borneo, across the South China Sea. Moving between these regions means crossing water, even while staying in the same country.

sections.title: A federation formed through history
sections.text: Malaysia was formed in 1963 by Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak, and Singapore. Singapore became independent in 1965. The remaining federation joins places with distinct local histories, rather than one continuous landmass.

stories.takeaway: Malaysia makes more sense as a federation of regions than as a single shape on a map.

stories.summary: A product’s brand tells you surprisingly little about where it was made.

sections.title: Start with components
sections.text: Malaysia’s electronics industry took root in the 1970s. International manufacturers and local firms built production networks that now range from semiconductor devices to industrial electronics.

sections.title: Specialize, then connect
sections.text: A chip passes through several stages before it reaches a device. Manufacturing, assembly, packaging, and testing depend on different skills. Malaysia’s role shows why industrial strength can be hidden inside a product carrying another country’s brand.

stories.takeaway: To understand a global industry, follow the work between countries as well as the finished product.

stories.question: What holds a diverse federation together?

paraphrases.question: What holds a diverse federation together?
phrasings: How does Malaysia stay united with so many different communities?
What keeps Malay, Chinese, Indian and Indigenous Malaysians in one country?
how do sabah and sarawak fit into malaysian identity?
Is there one typical Malaysian experience or does it vary by region?

stories.summary: A common national name does not mean a single regional experience.

sections.title: Many communities share the country
sections.text: Malay, Chinese, Indian, and many Indigenous communities contribute to Malaysian life. Sabah and Sarawak add histories and identities that cannot be understood only through the peninsula.

sections.title: Look beyond a national average
sections.text: The federal structure joins these regions within one state. Language, religion, local history, and economic opportunity still vary. Understanding those differences is a better starting point than expecting one typical Malaysian experience.

stories.takeaway: A federation is a way to share a country while retaining meaningful differences within it.
